title: Classify eight open cases by who attacked, why, and how they got in
situation: The security team has eight open cases, from a quiet data theft at a defense contractor to USB sticks left in a parking lot. Each case lists clues an analyst already gathered, such as 'demands payment' or 'used a valid account'. Leadership wants every case labelled with the type of attacker, their motive, and the way they got in, so the right fix goes to the right place.
your_task: Score each case's clues against the known attacker profiles (nation-state, organized crime, hacktivist, insider, unskilled attacker, shadow IT) and pick the best match.
Map the strongest clue to a motive, such as espionage, financial gain, revenge or blackmail.
Record the initial access vector (the way in), such as phishing email, default password or a phone call to the help desk.
List one fix for the way in, plus one extra control suited to that type of attacker.
why_it_matters: If you blame everything on a foreign government, you overspend and miss the simple holes, like default passwords. If you fix the malware but not the way it got in, the attacker walks back in next week.
done_when: All 8 cases have an attacker type, a motive and an entry vector, with the clues and scores that support each one.
Each case lists a fix for its entry vector and a control matched to the attacker.
The insider case (T-04) and the help-desk phone scam (T-08) are handed to the Identity and Access Management (IAM) team for access review and reset-procedure fixes.

glossary.Threat actor: The person or group behind an attack, such as a criminal gang or a disgruntled employee.
glossary.Nation-state / APT: A government-backed attacker; APT means advanced persistent threat, a well-funded attacker who stays hidden for a long time.
glossary.Hacktivist: An attacker who acts to promote a political or social cause.
glossary.Insider threat: A risk from someone who already has legitimate access, like an employee or contractor.
glossary.Shadow IT: Apps or services staff use without IT's approval, often with no bad intent.
glossary.Threat vector: The route an attacker uses to get in, such as email, a USB drive or a phone call.
glossary.Vishing: Voice phishing: tricking someone over the phone, for example into resetting a password.

talking_point: Classified 8 incidents by threat actor, motive and entry vector: 3 organized crime, 1 nation-state, 1 hacktivist, 1 insider, 1 unskilled attacker and 1 shadow IT case, and sent the insider and help-desk vishing cases to IAM for access and reset-process fixes.
